summary: Karpathy presents a detailed recipe for training neural networks, emphasizing that it is a leaky abstraction that fails silently, and advocating a patient, step-by-step process from data inspection to hyperparameter tuning.

claims.text: Neural net training is a leaky abstraction and fails silently, so a 'fast and furious' approach does not work.
claims.evidence_quote: a “fast and furious” approach to training neural networks does not work and only leads to suffering.

claims.text: The first step in training a neural net is to thoroughly inspect your data, spending hours scanning examples.
claims.evidence_quote: The first step to training a neural net is to not touch any neural net code at all and instead begin by thoroughly inspecting your data.

claims.text: At initialization, a softmax classifier should have a loss of -log(1/n_classes).
claims.evidence_quote: if you initialize your final layer correctly you should measure `-log(1/n_classes)` on a softmax at initialization.

claims.text: Using a fixed random seed ensures reproducibility and removes a factor of variation.
claims.evidence_quote: Always use a fixed random seed to guarantee that when you run the code twice you will get the same outcome.

claims.text: Overfitting a single batch of a few examples is a good test to verify the model can reach the lowest achievable loss.
claims.evidence_quote: Overfit a single batch of only a few examples (e.g. as little as two).

claims.text: Adam with a learning rate of 3e-4 is safe for early baselines.
claims.evidence_quote: In the early stages of setting baselines I like to use Adam with a learning rate of [3e-4].

claims.text: Adding more real training data is the best way to regularize a model.
claims.evidence_quote: the by far best and preferred way to regularize a model in any practical setting is to add more real training data.

claims.text: Random search is better than grid search for hyperparameter tuning.
claims.evidence_quote: it is best to use random search instead

claims.text: Model ensembles can gain about 2% accuracy on anything.
claims.evidence_quote: Model ensembles are a pretty much guaranteed way to gain 2% of accuracy on anything.

claims.text: Karpathy accidentally left a model training during winter break and it became state of the art.
claims.evidence_quote: One time I accidentally left a model training during the winter break and when I got back in January it was SOTA (“state of the art”).
